meta.title: useRef — accessing a DOM node imperatively

annotations.label: Component declaration
annotations.detail: FocusOnMount shows how to attach a ref to a real DOM node and read or mutate it imperatively — bypassing React's declarative data flow for operations that have no state equivalent.

annotations.label: Escape hatch for DOM
annotations.detail: useRef is React's sanctioned escape hatch. ref.current gives you the raw DOM node so you can call browser APIs (focus, scroll, measure, play/pause) that have no declarative equivalent.

annotations.label: inputRef is stable
annotations.detail: ref is the same object across renders; only .current changes. The handler always reads the latest DOM node, never a stale snapshot, because refs are mutable containers, not state.

steps.note: After the first render, ref.current points to the actual <input> DOM node.
